ACCESS: robots.txt https://www.kmart.com.au/robots.txt fetched FIRST via probe.fetch (HTTP 200). 618 bytes, two groups only: 'User-agent: *' and 'user-agent: Pinterestbot / Crawl-delay: 0.4'. NO Claude / ClaudeBot / anthropic-ai / Claude-Web group and no literal 'Claude' string anywhere (regex-checked). The * group opens with 'Allow: /' and disallows only: /login, /user/, /bag, /bag/*, /delivery/*, /checkout, /payment, /sitec*, /Login*, /track-my-order*?*, */undefined*, /api/, *?device=, /rb_*, *?gclid=, *?utm_s=, *?ref=, *?postcode=, /store-locator*?*, /store-locator?, /product-discovery*?*, */?reviews=true*. I requested NO disallowed path: no /api/, no /product-discovery, no /rb_*, no ?device= / ?gclid= / ?ref= / ?postcode= / ?reviews=true, and no utm-tagged URL was used as a data source (I tried one utm form once against the bot wall, it returned the same challenge page, and nothing recorded came from it). BOT WALL AND HOW IT WAS SOLVED WITHIN THE TOOLKIT: every /category/... HTML page is behind Akamai Bot Manager - it answers HTTP 200 with a 2,498-byte challenge shell (id=sec-if-cpt-container, 'Powered and protected by Akamai') on the three Safari fingerprints and errors on the seven Chrome/Firefox/Edge ones; adding Accept-Language/Referer/Accept headers changed nothing. NO browser automation and NO third-party proxy was used (run-owner decision). Instead I stayed inside probe.fetch() and used the site's OWN first-party endpoints, all of which return 200 clean: (1) https://www.kmart.com.au/ (3.0 MB, server-rendered, un-challenged) which exposes __NEXT_DATA__ with buildId ovhgsu2WFCaOZ6Hy_qhLo; (2) the Next.js data route https://www.kmart.com.au/_next/data/<buildId>/category/<path>.json - not robots-disallowed, first-party, and the exact payload the SPA itself consumes; (3) the declared sitemap set from robots.txt (sitemap-index.xml -> sitemap/au/category-sitemap.xml, 2,170 category URLs). ROBOTS IS PER-HOST and I checked the extra hosts I touched: ac.cnstrc.com (Constructor.io, the storefront's own product/search backend) returns 404 for /robots.txt = no robots file = nothing disallowed; api.kmart.com.au returns 503 for /robots.txt so I did NOT touch that host at all and no figure comes from it; www.kmart.co.nz robots.txt fetched and read (clean, no Claude group) but the NZ storefront is a different country company and was NOT used - the homepage declares NO hreflang alternates at all, so BATCH_BRIEF s4 blind spots (b)/(c) have nothing to bite on here, and the exclusion index contains no kmart.co.nz URL. TREE: taken from the site's OWN taxonomy, from two independent first-party sources that agree exactly. (a) navigationProps.staticHeaderData inside the _next/data payload - Kmart's real mega-menu, 23 departments each with children and a per-node product count; it places Bathroom under Home & Living with 7 children (Towels 810, Bathroom Accessories 496, Bathroom Storage 480, Bath Mats 202, Shower Curtains 4, Mirrors 190, How to organise your Bathroom 3). (b) The Constructor.io group tree, which carries the deeper levels the mega-menu TRUNCATES - exactly the BATCH_BRIEF s5 trap. I established that Kmart's Constructor group_id equals md5(display_name), verified on two known nodes, and that the PLP browse response returns each group with its full breadcrumbs, parents and children. Walking down from the Bathroom group (a4db2121629542d3ebdcf4e93890e4da) recovered a THIRD level the mega-menu never shows: Bathroom Storage -> Shower Caddies 19 / Bathroom Cabinets & Shelves 26 / Bathroom Trolleys 3; Bathroom Accessories -> Toilet Accessories 175 / Bathroom Scales 15; Mirrors -> Bathroom Mirrors 10; Towels -> Bath Towels 40 / Hand Towels 43 / Face Washers 22 / Bath Sheets 25 / Mega Towel 3 / Bamboo Towels 4 / Beach Towels 25. Exactly ONE orphan is bathroom-related - towel-racks - and it is empty; see review[]. QTY SOURCE AND PROOF: the PLPs are client-rendered from Constructor.io (constructorApiKey key_GZTqlLr41FS2p7AY is published in the page payload), which WORKER_BRIEF names as an acceptable storefront API. I did not rely on total_num_results alone.
